Switchgear shall be shipped by motor freight as completely assembled as

Progress reports shall be furnished to the Owner monthly, with each

Manufacturer ’s progress seriously fall behind his projected schedule.

Warranty provided by the Manufacturer  shall be understood to cover all
defects and problems related to the operation and maintenance of switchgear
for a minimum period of one (1) year from the date of commercial operation.
Manufacturer  guarantees that switchgear is capable of satisfactory and
continuous operation in accordance with Manufacturer ’s specifications and
Should the Owner detect any defects in design, or any problems with the
satisfactory operation of switchgear furnished under these specifications,
Owner will notify the Manufacturer  of the details related to the defect or
problem.  The Manufacturer  agrees to proceed with diligence in correction of
any problems as quickly as possible, particularly where the defect prevents
continuous operation of the switchgear.  Manufacturer ’s guarantee shall cover
the cost of replacement parts and repair, including “in-out” costs of loading,
transportation, and off-loading incurred by the Owner.
Owner will have right to operate equipment until all defects are corrected, and
guarantees met, without cost for depreciation, use or wear.
Switchgear may be removed from operation for examination, adjustment,
alteration, or change only at time approved by Owner.
Switchgear tests shall be performed in accordance with most current revision of
ANSI and IEEE test codes.  Manufacturer  shall notify Owner two (2) weeks
minimum in advance of switchgear testing to allow the standard performance
tests to be witnessed by Owner without additional cost to Owner (All
transportation and labor costs for Owner’s personnel will be covered by
Owner).  Test results shall include, but not necessarily be limited to, the
Hi-potential test on each pole with breaker contacts open.
Hi-potential test of switchgear bus assembly.
Contact resistance test (micro-ohms) for each pole of each circuit
Functional and operational tests of all power and control circuits.
CT and PT ratio and polarity test to verify integrity of Instrument
All tests shall be performed with installed equipment.  Manufacturer  shall
submit five (5) certified copies of all test data for each unit of switchgear
covered by these specifications, to the Owner.  Copies shall be included with
switchgear instruction manuals or bound in a form suitable for insertion into
If requested by the Owner as provided for in the Proposal Data Sheets, the
Manufacturer  shall provide a factory trained Field Service Engineer from the
Manufacturer of the switchgear building to supervise inspection, assembly and
testing of switchgear at the project site.
A visual inspection shall be performed by the Field Service Engineer, including
all accessories and parts disassembled and shipped separately to ensure that
the equipment was properly handled during transportation.  The Field Service
Engineer shall provide all necessary tools and special test equipment necessary
to perform standard check out procedures for switchgear and accessories.
Field Service Engineer shall also supervise and provide advice on the assembly
of switchgear.  Field Service Engineer shall have full authority to direct field
operations as necessary to assure that switchgear has been assembled and
service in accordance with Manufacturer ’s requirements.  After completion of
assembly, check electrical operation of accessories and instruct Owner’s
personnel on the operation and maintenance of equipment.
Cost for field service shall be as provided in the “Proposal Data Sheets”.  Field
service shall be scheduled only at the request of the Owner.  If field service trips
are necessary for the correction of defects or problems at no fault of the
Owner, such trips shall be at Manufacturer ’s expense.
The Manufacturer  is advised that the Owner may choose to accomplish field
tests to confirm any of the shop test results as an independent verification of
switchgear’s condition.  Should the Owner choose to perform such tests, it will
be conducted solely at the Owner’s expense.
Should field tests show discrepancies between Manufacturer ’s shop test results
and Owner’s field tests, or detect any irregularities in the ratings of equipment,
Manufacturer  shall assist the Owner in interpretation of results and any
corrective action necessary to achieve performance guarantees.
The Owner will evaluate bids, considering conformance with the specifications,
price, delivery, Manufacturer ’s reputation, optional services offered (such as
field assembly) and other items in the evaluation of proposals.  The Owner
reserves the right to waive or not waive any irregularities in the bid, to reject
any or all bids, and to determine which bid is the lowest and best bid for the
FAILURE TO MEET GUARANTEED DELIVERY DATE
Since delivery of switchgear specified herein is critical to the scheduling of the
Owner’s project, the Manufacturer  shall make every reasonable effort to meet
his guaranteed delivery date specified in the Summary of Proposal.
The Owner agrees to indemnify the Manufacturer  for circumstances beyond
the control of the Manufacturer .  Circumstances beyond the control of the
Manufacturer  are defined as: acts of God, acts of government, transportation
to final destination, failure of equipment under test, material shortages due to
failure of others to make delivery within the time usually required, and any
other circumstances reasonably beyond the control of the Manufacturer .
Upon any actual or projected departure from the manufacturing schedule (see
Section 1.7A.1) which, in the opinion of the Manufacturer , may result in delay
in shipment, the Manufacturer  shall immediately notify Owner of the following:
Explanation of delay or potential delay.
Means by which delay could be minimized.
Additional details as requested by the Owner.
Should the Manufacturer  fail to make a reasonable effort to meet the
guaranteed delivery date where this failure is evidenced by: failure to inform
the Owner of changes in the manufacturing schedule, failure to allow sufficient
time for delivery of materials and equipment necessary for manufacturing, or
lack of cooperation in effective measure by which delays could be minimized,
the Owner may penalize the Manufacturer  an amount not in excess of
$1,000.00 per calendar day for each day that the factory shipping date falls
beyond the guaranteed delivery date specified in the Summary of Proposal.
The Owner reserves the right to inspect the progress of work at the
Manufacturer ’s facilities at any time subsequent to notice of such intent.

coordinate with the applicable parties to assure proper implementation of all

limited to): SCADA, relay and CT wiring, overhead bus connection, and AC/DC

municipal power system to provide electrical service to residential, commercial
and light industrial loads via the City’s distribution system.
Switchgear will be connected to one substation type transformer by overhead
external rigid bus (by Owner). Switchgear shall include exterior roof top
bushings and bus support insulators for external buswork to be connected to
and supported above the switchgear building.

The breaker stationary unit shall have a set of primary disconnecting devices
